content:
I completely understand that my DIY iPhone lens hack looks pretty ridiculous — but it genuinely makes using my iPhone as a camera more practical and a lot more fun.

It started out as a solution to a video shoot I had coming up, but I've since found myself using it so many more times...

One of the biggest divides in the compact camera world is whether you need a viewfinder or not. Camera enthusiasts of a certain age will have strong opinions about electronic viewfinders (EVFs) versus optical ones, but EVFs are now good enough that very few people still care.

But regardless of optical or electronic, a viewfinder is a more practical way to shoot than using the rear screen, especially in bright sunlight. Even with the screen brightness turned up to maximum, it can be very difficult to see what you're shooting when the sun is strong, and screen glare is also an issue.

Although this hasn't historically been a huge problem in London, this summer's record-breaking heatwaves mean I honestly feel like the last time I saw a cloud or some rain was about 30 years ago.

But for me, the issue has an extra psychological dimension. I feel there's a difference, on a psychological level, between seeing the image in a frame, and seeing the world around you while taking the photo. Sometimes this sense of 'immersion' is the main reason I reach for a dedicated camera rather than my iPhone.

When I was choosing a video camera a few years ago, the Blackmagic Pocket Cinema Camera 4K was pretty much the only choice, but the lack of a viewfinder put me off. In the end I decided it wasn't a big problem for me, because I was mostly using it indoors, and even when using it outside, adding a big screen with a hood would solve most situations.

But sometimes I want to use it with something more portable, and I don't want an entire monitor rig, so I found a simple accessory that's good for outside use. It's a sun hood and magnifying loupe combo that magnetically attaches to the camera's rear screen, effectively giving you an optical viewfinder.

I have a shoot coming up where I need to use the BMPCC 4K alongside my iPhone 16 Pro Max for video. When I tested at the location, the viewfinder accessory was genuinely useful. Since the BMPCC 4K and iPhone screens are a similar size, I wondered if I could use it with my iPhone too.

Of course the iPhone doesn't have the magnets, but the iPhone is light enough that holding it manually against the loupe works perfectly. To my surprise, it works brilliantly, especially as I use the camera control button as a shutter.

Since then, I've used it in countless photo situations, and both the ability to see the screen better in bright sunlight and that sense of immersion have made shooting more enjoyable. My iPhone has long been my main camera, and this DIY hack has reinforced that, more often than not, the phone is more than good enough.

Ridiculous or inspired? Let me know in the comments. If you think the latter, unfortunately the accessory I bought has been discontinued, and I haven't seen anything else designed for screens bigger than three inches. If you find one, post a link in the comments.
